result.summary: ~/.claude (10 GB) is three things mixed in one folder. First, the dotclaude git repo, which tracks only a whitelist (.gitignore starts with `/*`). Second, three nested repos: skills/, global-memory/ and claude-memory-compiler/. Third, a large set of untracked items written by the Claude Code app and by plugins. The live config is small and current: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, settings.json, STORAGE.md, TOOLPATHS.md (re-verified 10-23), hooks/, scripts/, mods/ and agents/. Around it sits about 1 GB of leftovers: _windows-import-archive (930M), skills-archive (55M, tracked), doctor-backup-20260807 (23M), skills-backup-20260609, config/ (frozen Windows-era copies), 16 root-level .bak/backup files, the GSD/Vercel/model-router/LIFEOS remnants, and an orphaned node_modules (56M, nothing found that uses it). The root docs overlap heavily. RESTORE.md, START-HERE.md, MIGRATION-MACOS.md, RECOVERY-INVENTORY.md and restore.command/restore-README.txt all describe recovery, all are Windows-era or one-time, and none matches the current STORAGE.md backup model. Secrets handling is described in CREDENTIALS.md, TOOLPATHS.md 'Secrets', STORAGE.md and machine.md. rot.md exists as 3 identical copies. Some active config is gitignored with no other copy (output-styles/ELI5.md). Eric's own files sit inside app-owned folders (cache/recall-fts.sqlite, backups/doctor-plus-20260815). .git is 2.5 GB because session transcripts are committed daily, which Eric chose on 10-23 (feedback_session-history-tracked.md). result.area: Memory and knowledge stores (Tier B global-memory, Tier A project memory, claude-memory-compiler, memsearch, recall.py + bench, context-mode, SecondBrain counts, KeystoneOS outputs/registries)
result.summary: This area has 13 kinds of store an agent can write a fact to. They sit in roughly 60 physical folders, and on top of them are 5 copy or derived layers and 4 search indexes. The memory-write tier rules are clear, but four mechanisms keep creating second copies: (1) dev-sync/mirror_memory.py keeps a Windows twin of every Tier A folder; 11 pairs are byte-identical and the main ~/DEV pair is 23 files apart; memsearch still indexes 3 C--Users twins while recall.py picks the newest copy; (2) 8 Mac Tier A folders were made with '_' in the slug, but Claude Code 2.1.308 folds '_' to '-'. No session has ever loaded them, and memory-write SKILL.md:105 and remember.py still steer new writes into them; (3) harvest-dev-docs never prunes, so 43 of the 158 dev-docs folders are for archived or gone repos, and one is a copy of Linda_Projects' STATUS that ends up in the indexes; (4) a second global-memory clone at ~/DEV/claude-global-memory, 26 commits behind, is the copy of the global-memory STATUS that the indexes see. Facts also repeat across tiers: Tier A vs the compiled KB vs STORAGE.md/CLAUDE.md (the Drive FUSE hang is in 5+ places), and two Tier A slugs give the CFB forecast-capture cadence differently. Most of the compiler's 561M is its .venv (551M, of which 265M is a leftover Windows site-packages tree). The real content is small (daily 1.1M, knowledge 4.3M), and the only backup of daily/ and knowledge/ is the SSD layer: they are gitignored, not in the Drive .tgz set, and not in cloud-push. Where each kind of fact is true: user profile is USER.md; active threads, env and pending decisions are MEMORY.md; durable project, feedback and reference facts are the Mac Tier A slug (in practice -Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory); repo state is <repo>/docs/STATUS.md (dev-docs is only a mirror, so KeystoneOS docs belong in the KeystoneOS repo, which matches 64/64 files); session narrative is transcripts/; compiled daily and concepts are compiler daily/ and knowledge/ (derived, never the truth); Eric's own synthesis is the SecondBrain vault; decisions are KeystoneOS/decisions/log.md; the cross-harness view is unified-snapshot.md (regenerated). Three things have no true home: global-memory/handoffs (written, never indexed), Codex memory (empty DB, and the registry path is missing), and the no-twin OneDrive and G: slugs.

result.area: Agent records: audits, handoffs, status, logs, config backups
result.summary: Agent records are spread over about 25 homes, split across ~/.claude (dotclaude, global-memory, compiler), ~/DEV (the root thin repo, 119 repo docs/ folders, KeystoneOS), ~/SecondBrain and ~/Library/Logs. Every kind of record has a canonical-looking home: <repo>/docs/handoffs, <repo>/docs/STATUS.md, ~/.claude/scripts/logs plus the one alert channel .errors.log, and git history for config. Each also has live side-homes that tools cannot see. ~/DEV/docs/handoffs, ~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs (126 entries, 42 of them dead .windows twins) and ~/.claude/audits are not read by where-was-i.py and are not recall/memsearch roots. The harvested dev-docs mirror never prunes, so 43 archived repos stay indexed as if they were live. Growth is mostly unbounded: only daily-backup.ps1 caps its own log. everythingd.log went from 3.0 to 5.5 MB in about a day, shadow.jsonl from 4.6 to 5.6 MB, and STATUS bloat is a fleet problem (Flint 87 KB, TypeSafe_Sandbox 55 KB, PP_Recruiting 38 KB), while only the DEV root got an archive on 10-23. The .errors.log archive-then-clear step still lost lines on 10-23 (the dated archive is 0 bytes; the 9 lines survive only in git), and config .bak clutter is redundant with git (24 tracked in dotclaude, 11 untracked settings copies, 23 MB doctor-backup).
